CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is an 88-year-old male presenting with left arm pain that began approximately two weeks ago. He awoke at 2:00 AM with severe arm pain. He applied ice which provided some relief. He sat on the side of the bed and held his arm down to improve circulation without benefit. Pain resolved around 4-5 AM and he returned to sleep without recurrence that night. However, this pattern repeated over several nights. He was evaluated by another physician who suspected a pinched nerve. Pain radiates from the hand down the entire arm. He notes weakness in his hand, particularly with gripping. He reports that on days following nighttime pain, he experiences symptoms during the day as well. He was started on numbing medicine, a neck pill, and gabapentin by his previous provider, which have helped. Since starting these medications, he has not been significantly bothered at night. However, his hand continues to bother him. He notes that over the past week his neck has not been bothersome, but his hand remains symptomatic.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies neck pain with head turning or shoulder movement. Notes mild neck strain with head turning. Denies radicular pain. Hand weakness present, particularly with gripping. Reports prior injury to one finger that does not function properly. No apparent distress noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Neuropathy of lower extremities (VA service-connected, 1% disabled).
Cervical arthritis with disc degeneration.

MEDICATIONS
Gabapentin (frequency unclear, patient states he is unsure of dosage).
Eliquis.
Numbing medicine (as prescribed by previous provider).
Neck pill (specific medication not specified).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a veteran with service-connected disability related to lower extremity neuropathy. Currently using wheelchair for mobility. Lives with a female companion who assists with medication management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Elderly white male presenting in wheelchair, no apparent distress. Cervical range of motion: mild restriction in extension and right/left lateral rotation, symmetric, producing mild lateral neck pain without radicular pain. Cervical spine non-tender. Spurling's maneuver benign. Cranial nerves II-XII intact per template. Bilateral biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes 1+ bilaterally, all negative. Upper and lower extremity strength and sensation per template. Gait not assessed. Grip strength intact bilaterally. Sensation intact bilaterally in hands.

RESULTS
Cervical X-ray (6421): Significant disc degeneration at C5-C6, to a lower extent at C4-C5 and C3-C4. Significant lower cervical facet arthropathy at C6-C7 and C7-T1, difficult to visualize on current imaging. MRI of cervical spine pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left upper extremity neuropathy suspicious for cervical radiculopathy, possibly with contribution of peripheral neuropathy. Plan: Cervical MRI to identify exact location of nerve root compression. Tentatively plan for left C7-T1 epidural steroid injection pending MRI results to provide focused anti-inflammatory treatment. Continue home exercise program. Continue gabapentin twice daily. Follow up after epidural to assess symptom relief.

2. Neck pain in the setting of cervical arthritis and disc degeneration. Continue current management.

Patient agreeable to proposed plan. Denies use of blood thinners.
